She says, Clarence is bad enough, but that Elmer, she says, he is impossible.

segments.speaker: Frank Rowan
segments.words: And they're small men too.

segments.speaker: Lottie Rowan
segments.words: Clarence was working over in the field. I like to be up there in the house where we lived. Then I'd look out across over on the down toward the canyon. And it was an awful hot and sultry day. And you know, there's a difference between a day of being just real hot and a day that's hot and you just can't hardly breathe. And he always had a whip. He was farming with horses at that time. And they were still with horses anyway. And he was going with a whip and hollering at them with a whip. And so he was going around around fields like that. And I thought, my goodness, the way you're crowding those horses, if you don't kill them, it's going to be funny, a day like this. So about a half an hour or so, I looked over there and I seen a big smoke over in the, just out of the field and over in the brush there, big fire going. Smoke coming out of there. And of course, I didn't know what was happening. I didn't see the horse fall or didn't know what it was. And found out after it's that he just crowded the horses and this horse could take them and he just dropped dead. So I suppose he went to the house then and maybe his brother just come down for some reason. But they drug that horse over into the brush and burned it over there. And oh, was his wife mad at him. Oh, she says, I am so mad at Clarence. I don't know what I could do to him. She says, that poor horse, just crowded and crowded. And she says, I just always thought him about the way he treats his animals, crowding them in the hot weather. And she says, this ought to be a lesson to him. But she says, oh, I don't suppose it will be. But they didn't farm with horses very long after that. They got a tractor.
